Run it ONLY as: /workspace/dataset/test19_executable <args>    (never use `python`; it is not available)
The program's source is:

    import argparse
    from bidict import bidict
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--k1', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--v1', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--k2', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--v2', type=int, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    b1 = bidict({args.k1: args.v1, args.k2: args.v2})
    b2 = b1.copy()
    print(b2)
    b1['new'] = 999
    print(b1)
    print(b2)
    result = b2.inv[args.v1]
    print(result)

Goal: a Node.js reimplementation must match stdout, stderr and exit code character-for-character.
Use bash. Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY when it matters, e.g.:
  /workspace/dataset/test19_executable --k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 >/tmp/o.txt 2>/tmp/e.txt; echo "RC=$?"; then inspect with od -c or cat -A.
Run MANY probes (30+). Be systematic and adversarial: hunt for cases where a naive JS port would differ.
Report ONLY hard empirical findings you actually observed, each with the exact command and the exact bytes of output.
Do not speculate about Python internals you did not observe.


Resolve this ONE open question empirically by running the executable. Be exhaustive on this narrow point.

OPEN QUESTION: Is there any input where line 4 (`print(result)`) FAILS to encode? sys.stdout appears to use errors='surrogateescape' (byte 0xff round-trips). Try to find a counterexample by getting a surrogate outside the DC80-DCFF range into a key — probably impossible via argv, but worth one attempt: `/workspace/dataset/test19_executable --k1=$(printf '\xed\xa0\x80') --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 | od -An -tx1` (observed: decodes to three surrogateescapes and re-emits `ed a0 80`). Confirm no UnicodeEncodeError path exists.

Return the definitive answer with exact commands and exact output bytes (use od -c where escapes matter), plus the implementable rule for a JS port.

content.text: Byte 0x33 was a transient PyInstaller temp-dir flake. Now a rigorous sweep with `k2=K2` to avoid key collisions, plus retry-on-flake.

input.command:
rm -rf /tmp/sw2 && mkdir -p /tmp/sw2 && bad=""; flake=""
for i in $(seq 1 255); do
  hex=$(printf '%02x' $i)
  printf "\\x$hex" > /tmp/sw2/in_$hex
  printf "\\x$hex\n" > /tmp/sw2/exp_$hex
  for try in 1 2 3; do
    /workspace/dataset/test19_executable --k1="$(cat /tmp/sw2/in_$hex)" --v1 1 --k2 K2 --v2 2 >/tmp/sw2/o_$hex 2>/tmp/sw2/e_$hex
    rc=$?
    grep -q 'PYI-' /tmp/sw2/e_$hex || break
    flake="$flake $hex"
  done
  # last line of stdout (2 bytes expected: byte + \n)
  n=$(wc -c < /tmp/sw2/exp_$hex)
  tail -c "$n" /tmp/sw2/o_$hex > /tmp/sw2/got_$hex
  if ! cmp -s /tmp/sw2/got_$hex /tmp/sw2/exp_$hex; then bad="$bad $hex(rc=$rc)"; fi
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then bad="$bad RC$hex=$rc"; fi
done
echo "MISMATCHES:$bad"; echo "FLAKES:$flake"

content.text: Now a large randomized fuzz to prove the round-trip is universal.

input.command:
rm -rf /tmp/fz && mkdir -p /tmp/fz; bad=0; n=0
for t in $(seq 1 220); do
  len=$(( (RANDOM % 8) + 1 ))
  # random non-NUL bytes
  head -c 200 /dev/urandom | tr -d '\000' | head -c $len > /tmp/fz/in
  sz=$(wc -c < /tmp/fz/in); [ "$sz" -eq 0 ] && continue
  k1=$(cat /tmp/fz/in)          # note: strips trailing newlines
  printf '%s' "$k1" > /tmp/fz/in2
  sz2=$(wc -c < /tmp/fz/in2); [ "$sz2" -eq 0 ] && continue
  # skip collisions with k2/new
  [ "$k1" = "K2" ] && continue; [ "$k1" = "new" ] && continue
  for try in 1 2 3; do
    /workspace/dataset/test19_executable --k1="$k1" --v1 1 --k2 K2 --v2 2 >/tmp/fz/o 2>/tmp/fz/e; rc=$?
    grep -q 'PYI-' /tmp/fz/e || break
  done
  n=$((n+1))
  printf '\n' >> /tmp/fz/in2
  exp=$(wc -c < /tmp/fz/in2)
  tail -c "$exp" /tmp/fz/o > /tmp/fz/got
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || [ -s /tmp/fz/e ] || ! cmp -s /tmp/fz/got /tmp/fz/in2; then
    bad=$((bad+1)); echo "MISMATCH rc=$rc in=$(od -An -tx1 /tmp/fz/in2|tr -s ' \n' ' ') got=$(od -An -tx1 /tmp/fz/got|tr -s ' \n' ' ')"
    cp /tmp/fz/in2 /tmp/fz/bad_$t; cp /tmp/fz/o /tmp/fz/bado_$t; cp /tmp/fz/e /tmp/fz/bade_$t
  fi
done
echo "FUZZ: tested=$n mismatches=$bad"
